independence: Initial frontend source inspection was independent of this reviewer's earlier style-tooling work. After reporting concrete defects, the parent explicitly authorized this reviewer to implement frontend remediations and regressions. Those remediations are therefore self-reviewed here, not independently approved changes.
scope: accepted source and draft presentation freshness

findings.title: Untrusted drop identifiers could invent undeclared references and inject generated source
findings.original_evidence: Workbench insert accepted every text/plain value beginning ref: and called reference(item.slice(4)) without validating identifier spelling or membership in state.names. renderExpr inserted the name directly into Alloy source.
findings.impact: An external drag payload could bypass the declared-symbol palette and change the generated candidate's structure. Server parsing of the resulting text cannot by itself establish correspondence with the advertised composer tree.
findings.remediation: model.paletteNode now resolves only closed known palette operators or exact declared names that also satisfy validName. Workbench rejects undefined resolutions before invalidation/tree mutation. The generated-source path no longer accepts raw untrusted reference text.
findings.regression: Tests reject the source-injection string, univ, missing symbols, malformed declared names and unknown operators while preserving legitimate palette/reference construction.
findings.limitations: The synthetic generated-source counterexample was inspected as exact text; this reviewer did not run that original payload through the Alloy parser or a real browser drag operation.

findings.title: Cancellation failures could overwrite a newer draft notice; successful cancellation lacked full source/job identity checks
findings.original_evidence: Workbench cancel catch unconditionally called setNotice. Its successful path checked revision and epoch only, omitting jobId and sourceHash. A pending cancellation failure arriving after a text edit could replace the new draft notice.
findings.remediation: api.sameIdentity compares all four jobId/sourceHash/revision/epoch fields. api.cancelSnapshot captures the requested identity and suppresses stale success and failure outcomes. Workbench maintains the active job source hash, passes a current-identity reader, and rechecks identity before applying either result or error notice. Invalidation clears the active identity synchronously.
findings.regression: Real API cancellation orchestration is exercised with deferred mocked fetch promises: matching current cancellation, successful response after raw edit, failed response after raw edit, failed response after active job change, wrong-source/wrong-job response, and a still-current failure. Tests make no real HTTP requests.

additional_hardening.change: waitJob now compares full active identity on each intermediate poll and terminal response.
additional_hardening.assessment: Before remediation, sourceHash was checked before initial display and again before terminal display, so intermediate hash omission did not by itself demonstrate a wrongly displayed terminal result. The added check rejects a mismatched intermediate response earlier and keeps polling bound to the original active source.

positive_assessments: Type mismatches leave the candidate tree unchanged, explicit holes block application, and formula/relation constructors use a closed palette. Authoritative Alloy validation remains the server boundary.

Composer validation commits source/revision only on a current VALIDATED result. Free text edits clear results, advance the synchronous epoch and hide the prior block projection in explicit text-only mode.
execute hashes exact TextEncoder UTF-8 bytes, validates the first returned source hash and revision/epoch, and verifies a source-bound terminal identity before committing or displaying a result.

consumeToken extracts authority from the fragment and immediately replaces browser history with pathname/search, retaining the token in module/component memory. The unit test checks replaceState; real browser history/referrer behavior was not exercised here.

Results distinguishes SAT run instances from SAT check counterexamples and labels UNSAT absence within bounds. UNKNOWN and TIMEOUT remain inconclusive outcomes; the persistent disclaimer rejects unbounded-proof interpretation.

Authored frontend callable documentation and <=30-line checks pass. Immutable node shapes, copied child arrays and hook-local state keep mutable UI state behind module/component interfaces. These are coding checks and inspection, not a universal alias/dataflow proof.

checks.result: Vitest unit tests passed, including actual deferred cancellation orchestration and forged palette reference rejection.
Full authored JS/TS/TSX and test inventory passed after remediation.

limitations: No browser or accessibility/screen-reader QA was performed by this reviewer. Browser keyboard construction, real drag/drop, invalid-edit/late-result and fragment-removal workflows remain assembled acceptance evidence.
No concurrent full build, bundled artifact rebuild, Java integration test or real server/solver job was run during this frontend review; the parent owns the final assembled build.
The added deferred tests exercise the exported cancellation orchestration rather than mounting React. Wiring and synchronous identity invalidation were inspected directly.

The reduced composer exposes formula versus relation slots over the declared unary subset; it does not demonstrate full Alloy nominal/subtyping/arity block coverage or the later G2/G3 round-trip gate.
